title: Make a design's declared architecture_rules reach Fitness (.taad/fitness.yaml)
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1: .taad/fitness.yaml exists: missing

C2: fitness.yaml carries the five FsAnalyser rules (screen-free Core; only the classifier reads the reparse attribute, widened; directories listed only through DirectoryReader; counting-rule tests never skipped, extended; interop only in Native): missing
C3: a mechanism turns a design's declared architecture_rules into fitness.yaml, so later slices are gated: missing
C4: the Fitness gate no longer reads 'no rules declared' (Fitness op=check evaluates rules instead of NONE): missing

Does the person accept SL-022 as closing C1, C2, C4 and the effect of C3, while the mechanism half of C3 (design._append_rules in taad_v3) is verified and committed on its own? The engine's append was measured only on a working-tree copy with design.py uncommitted, and SL-020 declared four rules that never produced a file. Or should the C3 criterion be reworded, or an engine-side obligation filed?

Is any other filesystem-analyser-v2 slice in flight that has declared, or will declare, architecture_rules before SL-022 merges? Its design would append to, and so create, the same file with different content. The add/add conflict at commit-slice's refresh is one nothing resolves.

Eight split entries with exact rooted scopes (the proposal, and spike 1's 'exact scopes' option) versus five superset-scope entries (spike 1's other option, which runs .cs patterns over .csproj and .resx) versus six (spike 4's rooted translation, which splits only the interop rule). I chose eight because it is the only form that keeps each xUnit scope exact.

Two copies of the rules (yaml plus xUnit, kept in step by a header comment) versus a single source, where the test loads the yaml or a generator writes both. Rejected here as over-built for a low-risk slice, but drift has no mechanical guard.

Hand-writing the five rules versus declaring them in this design's architecture_rules so the engine's append writes them, which would exercise C3 end to end. Rejected because the record has no including_comments, so comment-only violations false-pass, and the append path is unmeasured with a non-empty list.
Naming entries as the xUnit method name plus a glob suffix, versus one plain name per rule with duplicated names across the split entries.
Leaving the mechanism half of C3 to the engine versus building a project-side converter. The over_engineering_flag pushed against the converter.

No entries in `cases`. The design keeps any converter, parity test or YAML parser out of the .NET project, and no project test feeds a fitness.yaml shape. Pointing at the xUnit twin would claim coverage it does not give. Each shape was measured in a scratch harness instead, as the design prescribed, and the commands and results are listed under `tests`: case 1 (op=rules, plus controls showing a double-quoted `\b` silently stops matching and a double-quoted `\s` makes the loader refuse the file), case 2 (git check-ignore), cases 3-8 and 12 (17 plants and controls), case 9 (coverage counts plus…
The mechanism half of C3 (design._append_rules in taad_v3) is engine code outside this worktree. Per Q-009 it is not an SL-022 criterion. I only measured it (O-004, O-005).

C4 is shown with the engine's own fitness module run from the shell, not with the Fitness MCP tool, which the builder is not granted. The design closes C4 only when the '8 rule(s) checked … Every declared rule holds' text appears in this slice's own validate record.
Case 13 (a slice cut before this merges reads NONE) has nothing to build. The design marked it non-material.
Case 14 (a later design appends onto this file) cannot be run through a real design from this repo. It was measured by calling the engine's `_append_rules` on a scratch copy (O-004).

The line number is off for the using-directive rule. `(?m)^\s*using…` matched against whole-file text starts at the first blank line before the offending line: a plant at Scanner.cs:7 after a blank line was reported at :6, while xUnit said :7. Fitness and xUnit still fail on the same rule and file. Fixing it means changing both copies of the rule (for example to `^[ \t]*`), which touches ArchitectureRulesTests and is outside this slice.

Fitness matches `\s`, `[^)]*` and `[^>]*` across line breaks, and xUnit matches one line at a time. That makes Fitness a strict superset: it can fire on a multi-line attribute or project reference that xUnit misses. It is noted in the file header, and nothing in the current tree triggers it.

Engine side (taad_v3): compile must_not_match with MULTILINE, or have the append carry including_comments, so rules a design declares do not silently match less than hand-written ones. Also, the append writes CRLF in text mode on Windows, so the file ends up with mixed line endings. It still loads, and git autocrlf normalises the blob.

Fitness prunes build output only by directory name, so a gitignored directory nested inside a rooted scope (for example src/artifacts/) is read. xUnit reads it too, so the two agree. Honouring .gitignore in the engine would close this.
There is no mechanical guard against the yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs drifting apart. Only the header comment names the twin. The design accepted this risk.
Case 11 is a no-op: no pattern has a `$` anchor. Also, the engine opens files in text mode (fitness.py:422), which already turns CRLF into LF, so even a `$` anchor would work without `\r?`.
Remember that `python -m taad3.fitness --op check` exits 0 even when it prints VIOLATED. Any gate built on it must read the report text.
